Subject: Pilot headroom reservation request — Lakeview Health POC

Team —

Quick ask: Lakeview (Zephyr Health) is kicking off a 3-week POC next Tuesday and they want guaranteed headroom for high-concurrency inference during upload/ingestion windows. Product wants a short reservation rather than relying purely on burst autoscale. TL;DR: 8 x A100-class GPU equivalents reserved for 21 days, with an autoscale policy exception to allow pre-warming and a static minimum that overrides soft-eviction for the pilot window.

Why: the POC runs a mix of chat + long-document embeddings (seq len ~4k for some requests) and we saw unpredictable cold-starts during their sandbox run. Lakeview is evaluating latency tail and throughput stability — losing tokens to queueing will derail the case study.

Asks (need by EOD Monday):
- Ops: confirm if we can carve 8 GPU equiv (zone us-west-2) and pin them to the Lakeview pilot for 2027-09-14 — 2027-10-05.
- Infra: what telemetry/alerts will we surface (cost burn, pre-warm fail, eviction attempts)?
- Finance/Sales: cost estimate and short approval path so Legal can sign the SOW attached.

I've attached the pilot_resource_plan.xlsx with estimated qps, concurrency, and model variants.

Thanks —
Kim
Kimberly Park
Product Lead, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot headroom reservation request — Lakeview Health POC

Kim —

Thanks for the context. A few clarifying Qs before I commit capacity:
1) Model and instance profile: which model family and quantization level? Is this gpt-large fp16 or a 4-bit quantized variant? That changes GPU memory and packing dramatically.
2) Request distribution: you mention ingestion windows — what are the expected 1-minute and 5-minute peak qps, and expected sustained concurrency outside peaks?
3) KV cache size / max seq: you noted ~4k for some requests; are those outliers or the norm? If we need long KV caching, one A100 equiv might only support fewer concurrent streams.
4) Fallback tolerance: if we can't pin all 8 GPU equiv, are we OK with a hybrid (4 reserved + 4 burst) and automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model?

Operationally, two options:
A) Reserve a dedicated slice (8 equiv) and apply an autoscale-exempt policy for the window (hard minimum + soft eviction disabled). This guarantees performance but triggers billing and stewardship approvals.
B) Place them in a burst buffer with elevated pre-warm priority and build a targeted cache-warm routine — cheaper but higher risk for tail latency at day 1.

If you want me to pursue (A) I need model/quant info and a firm go-live timestamp by EOD Monday so I can update the capacity calendar and open the reservation ticket with CloudOps.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
